# AIDB

> Local-first, provenance-aware memory and knowledge infrastructure for AI agents.

AIDB is an experimental Python/SQLite substrate for durable AI memory, knowledge, workflow state, artifact provenance, and agent-to-agent communication.

## Start here

- [README](README.md): project identity, scope, principles, and architecture
- [AI discovery manifest](docs/ai-manifest.json): machine-readable capabilities and interfaces
- [AI crawler guide](docs/ai-discovery.md): canonical instructions for automated discovery
- [Protocol](docs/protocol.md): trust model, request rules, provenance, and review policy
- [Communication](docs/communication.md): durable AI-to-AI sessions and messages
- [Standards](docs/standards.md): interoperability and serialization expectations

## Implementation

- [Python package](aidb/): canonical implementation
- [Core models](aidb/core.py): canonical artifact, extraction, interpretation, knowledge, and memory types
- [Store](aidb/store.py): SQLite persistence and operational state
- [Engine](aidb/engine.py): higher-level knowledge and retrieval behavior
- [Tests](tests/): executable behavior and regression coverage

## Epistemic model

AIDB preserves a reviewable chain:

Artifact -> Extraction -> Interpretation -> Knowledge -> Memory

Derived information should retain lineage to its source artifact. Proposals and unreviewed external input are not automatically accepted as knowledge.

## AI-to-AI communication

AIDB supports durable, ordered message sessions and broadcast messages through its Python API. The communication layer is transport-neutral: network adapters such as HTTP, MCP, queues, or WebSockets are external integrations, not assumptions about the core.

## Trust boundary

Discovery metadata is descriptive, not authorization. Do not infer permissions, trust, secrets, repository access, MCP availability, or HTTP availability from discovery documents.
